messages:
Anna: Heads up — Acadia sent back their vendor security questionnaire and flagged our data deletion + KMS sections. They want clear language on deletion workflows for hosted vs dedicated. Attached file: Acadia_Vendor_Form.pdf

Anna: They want an answer by EOD tomorrow — this is a renewal blocker (month-to-month trial). Can we draft something concise? :eyes:

Mike: Can you paste the exact question? If it's about deletion we should link to the retention & deletion docs and call out KMS. Also note legal may need to sign off.

Anna: Quote from their form: "How does Redwood ensure customer data is deleted on request across hosted and dedicated deployments, including backups and key management? Please include timelines and auditability."

Leah: Short note from infra side: for hosted we expose a Delete API + internal workflows; primary storage purge within 24 hours of request, backups rotated/deleted as per backup retention (we usually target 30d). For Dedicated we provide a deletion runbook and can coordinate a one-time purge job; if customer manages keys we remove access and provide proof. I'll draft a blurb.

Mike: Add that deletions are recorded in our audit logs (Console -> Activity) and that for Private/Dedicated customers we support customer-managed CMKs (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). For Hosted, we use Redwood-managed KMS and can provide attestations of key rotation and access controls. Avoid absolute guarantees on backups — use "within" language.

Leah: Draft blurb (please review):

Leah: "Hosted: Customers may request deletion via the Delete API (POST /v1/customers/{id}/delete) or by contacting support. Primary data in active storage is removed within 24 hours of a validated request. Backups are rotated and deleted in accordance with our backup retention policy (typically within 30 days); we provide deletion entries in the tenant audit log for traceability. KMS: Hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys; access to keys is restricted to authorized systems and logged.

Dedicated/Private: For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide a documented deletion runbook and, on request, will execute a coordinated purge. Customers using customer-managed keys (CMKs) can disable or rotate keys to render encrypted data inaccessible; we can provide confirmation artifacts. All deletion actions are logged and can be included in an evidence package for audits.

Notes: Specific timelines may vary by deployment and retention settings. Please contact support or your CS rep to schedule a purge and request evidence."

Julian: I'll send that to Acadia with links to our SOC2 summary and the DPA. Can someone thumbs-up if the wording is okay? This will unblock renewal. :thumbsup:

Mike: Quick tweak suggestion: change "within 24 hours" to "within 24 hours of request for primary storage" and replace "typically within 30 days" with "within 30 days" to avoid implying faster guarantees. Also add a line: "We do not retain customer PII in logs — operational logs are redacted/hashed."

Leah: Updated blurb pasted (final):

Leah: "Hosted: Customers may request deletion via the Delete API (POST /v1/customers/{id}/delete) or by contacting support. Primary data in active storage is removed within 24 hours of a validated request. Backups are deleted in line with our backup retention policy and are removed within 30 days. Deletion events are recorded in tenant audit logs for traceability. Hosted customers use Redwood-managed keys; key management actions are logged and monitored.

Dedicated/Private: For Dedicated and Private deployments we provide a documented deletion runbook and can execute a coordinated purge on request. Customers using customer-managed keys can disable or rotate CMKs to render encrypted data inaccessible; we provide confirmation artifacts where applicable. All deletion actions are logged and can be included in an evidence package for audits.

Additional notes: We do not retain customer PII in raw operational logs (logs are redacted/hashed). For requests requiring signed legal confirmation, please loop in @sara_legal. Timelines depend on retention configuration and deployment model."

Leah: API example for CS reply (paste into their form if they want technical steps):

Leah: ```http
POST /v1/customers/abcd/delete
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "reason": "data deletion request",
  "requester": "admin@acadia.com"
}
```

Julian: Looks good. Sending now and CCing Legal in case they ask for signed artifacts. I'll link our DPA and the subprocessor list: https://redwood.example.com/subprocessors

OnboardingBot: Uploaded file "acadia_reply_draft_v1.pdf" to thread.

Anna: Thanks team. FYI I've noted renewal risk and will flag to Rev Ops if they don't respond within 48h. Julian please paste their reply here so we can track follow-ups.

Julian: Sent — they asked one follow-up about whether we can provide a signed statement of deletion for backups. Tagging @sara_legal to advise.

sara_legal: I can draft a one-line attestation if needed but prefer to limit language to "evidence of deletion actions" rather than absolute statements about backups. I'll prepare language and post here by EOD.

Anna: Perfect. Appreciate the quick turnaround everyone.
